q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of an emergency light?
title: Emergency light carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the plastic body, LED board, battery, charger circuit and adapter per unit and multiply by supplier figures. Add moulding and assembly energy, then divide the plant's energy by units made.

ul: Final assembly, charging test and packing.

p: Report per unit by battery type and capacity. The battery is often the largest part of the figure.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 14,200 / 50,000 = 0.284 kg CO2 per unit
Add battery, LED board and plastics for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
